content:
marie (CS): Hey team, customer 'Acme Health' on Dedicated (private VPC) reporting streaming responses cutting off mid-chunk and clients doing repeated reconnects. They see partial text then a reconnect. Root cause unclear.
acme-sre: Confirmed. Happens ~5-10% of requests. Client is internal app behind corporate proxy. Repro: long SSE stream (500-800 tokens) truncates after a few chunks, client reconnects and resumes, sometimes duplicates last chunk.
marie (CS): They pasted logs from our gateway:
```
2026-04-02T15:23:12Z INFO request id=abc123 start stream
2026-04-02T15:23:14Z WARN backend write: short write (wrote 512 of 1024)
2026-04-02T15:23:14Z ERROR upstream broken pipe: write tcp 10.2.1.5:443 -> 10.2.8.9:54832: write: connection reset by peer
```
acme-sre: Their client logs show a TLS close with TCP RST and then a reconnect almost immediately. No auth errors. Token refresh looks fine.
ben (eng-runtime): Is the proxy terminating TLS or doing any buffering/chunk coalescing? Fragmented frames could be getting dropped if MTU mismatch + proxy TCP window issues.
sophia (eng-network): Very possible. Corporate proxies we see in the wild (ASA/F5/BlueCoat) sometimes buffer and reassemble chunks; if client path MTU is lower than server's MSS we get fragmentation. If middlebox doesn't handle reassembly+streaming properly you see truncated SSE payloads.
kevin (devex): Do we have a minimal repro curl command the customer can run? If we can reproduce locally it's way easier than chasing corp-proxy configs.
acme-sre: Yep, here's repro they ran from behind proxy (curl via corp proxy):
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://dedicated.acme.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-xyz"
# output:
# data: {"id":"tok1","text":"Hello from Redwood ...\n"}
# data: {"id":"tok2","text":"The next chunk starts but is truncated"
# <connection reset, then curl reconnects>\n
```
marie (CS): They also ran a direct test from a jumpbox in the same VPC (no corp proxy) and the stream completes fine every time.
ben (eng-runtime): That strongly points to intermediate proxy. Two things to check: 1) MTU/MSS on path, 2) proxy buffering/timeout settings and whether it closes idle TCP connections during long idle gaps between chunks.
sophia (eng-network): Ask them to run these quick checks:
- ping to gateway with large payloads to test PMTU: `ping -M do -s 1472 <ip>` (expect fragmentation if fails)
- tcpdump on client side to check for TCP RST/FIN around truncation
- check proxy logs for 502/504 or buffer-related messages
acme-sre: We ran `ping -M do -s 1472` and it failed, but `-s 1400` works. So PMTU inferred ~1400.
kevin (devex): Good. Workarounds:
- Lower MTU on client interface to 1400
- Configure proxy to allow chunked transfer and disable buffering for the route (nginx: `proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on;`)
- Increase keepalive and tune proxy timeouts
- Client-side: add reconnect-idempotency so duplicates are deduplicated on resume
carlos (billing): Side note - customer mentioned a spike in tokens billed due to duplicate resumed streams; we should advise on dedupe and offer credits if we confirm duplicate output caused by reconnects under our hosted routing. I'll hold off until engineering confirms root cause.
sophia (eng-network): For long-term fix: if the proxy is dropping fragmented TCP frames due to MTU, they need to either fix PMTU (ICMP allowed), lower MTU, or ensure the proxy does not re-chunk the application payload. On some appliances there is a config like 'streaming mode' or 'disable buffering'.
ben (eng-runtime): From runtime side we can make two improvements:
1) Tolerate chunk boundary splits better — ensure we don't treat partial chunk as terminal and keep state for immediate resume de-dup.
2) Add more logging to detect upstream mid-chunk closes and surface a specific 'mid-stream-reset' metric so CS can correlate with customer-proxy events.
marie (CS): Customer is willing to apply workaround (lower MTU / disable proxy buffering) but asked if we can do any immediate mitigation on our side to stop duplicate tokens and charge spikes.
ben (eng-runtime): Short term: we can add server-side dedupe for immediate N tokens after resume per-request-id, but that's not trivial and risks hiding legit replays. Better to offer credits for duplicated tokens while we work a proper fix.
marie (CS): acme-sre, please attach tcpdump and any proxy logs. We'll schedule a 1:1 debug session with eng-runtime + network tomorrow.
acme-sre: Attached a pcap (sent via secure link) and proxy logs. PCAP shows MSS 1460 from server, but client ACKs show segments with 1400 data. There's an occasional RST from proxy IP right when truncated chunk arrives.
infra-bot: Incident link created: INC-2026-4577 (investigate dedicated streaming truncation for Acme Health)
ben (eng-runtime): I'll pick this up tomorrow AM. Plan: reproduce with a test proxy that simulates MTU=1400 + buffering to capture the exact boundary behavior. If we can reproduce we can add a small runtime patch to be more robust to chunk splits within boundaries.
kevin (devex): I'll prepare a KB article for customers behind corporate proxies describing: - MTU checks - proxy buffering flags - curl reproducible steps - how to reduce MTU temporarily
carlos (billing): If engineering confirms duplicates caused by reconnect/resume we can offer a one-time credit. Keep me posted.
marie (CS): Thanks all. Next steps: acme-sre will confirm a test window and provide pcap link; ben/sophia will run reproducer; kevin will draft KB. We'll update thread after the debug session. :thumbsup:
acme-sre: Thanks, appreciated. We'll be on stand-by for the debug call.
